# Fitness status — 2026-10-02

Window: 2026-09-19 to 2026-10-02 (14 days)

## Summary

**Training load & consistency.** 9 activities in the 14 days: 6 runs (43.7 km, 371 min) and 3 road rides (147.8 km, 459 min), about 13 h 50 min in total. Running split evenly across the two halves of the window: 23.0 km in 19-25 Sep (Mont Bre hill run 7.95 km on 20 Sep, 6.01 km on 21 Sep, 9.01 km on 25 Sep) and 20.7 km in 26 Sep-2 Oct (5.35 km on 26 Sep, 10.34 km on 29 Sep, and the 5.01 km tempo on 30 Sep at about 6:24/km, average HR 138, aerobic TE 3.5, load 113). Rides were on 19 Sep (50.4 km), 23 Sep (43.4 km) and 27 Sep (54.0 km). 1 Oct was a full rest day with no activity and only 718 steps, so load is easing off slightly. Acute load fell from 452 to 380 against a chronic load of 372 (ratio 1.0, optimal). Training status is still "productive", as it has been since 20 Sep. Load balance still flags a high-aerobic shortage: 185 against a target of 409-737. Low-aerobic is 1193 against 191-518, and anaerobic is 46 against 109-327.

**Recovery signals.** Readiness this morning (09:09) is 62, moderate. Recovery time is essentially zero (recovery factor 99%), but the sleep factor dropped to 53% and the HRV factor to 79%. Load ratio is 90%, stress history 97% and sleep history 68%. A provisional reading just after midnight was 75 (high), and it fell once the night was scored. Last night was short and late. Bedtime was 01:29 and wake-up 08:35, giving 6 h 24 min of sleep with a score of 69: 58 min deep, only 37 min REM, 289 min light and 42 min awake. Over the window, sleep averaged 7.5 h, but 5 of 14 nights were under 6.5 h (23, 26, 28 and 30 Sep, plus last night). Overnight HRV was 38 ms, below the 45-55 baseline and matching the window low (also 38 on 28 Sep). The weekly average slipped to 45, at the bottom edge of the baseline, though status is still "balanced", as it has been every day in the window. Resting HR is 53, against a usual 49 (7-day average 50). That ties the window high, last seen on 21 Sep, the day after the Mont Bre run. Body battery was 69 at wake-up, against 90 yesterday. Average stress so far today is 25, inside the 15-46 range of the 14-day daily averages. Today's stats are partial because the day is still in progress. SpO2 averages are not populated for any day in the window.

**VO2max trend.** Per-run readings: 21 Sep 40, 25 Sep 41, 26 Sep 41, 29 Sep 41, 30 Sep 41. The 20 Sep Mont Bre run has no value. The account-level figure is populated and was last updated 30 Sep at 41.1 (precise value). No run since then, so there is no new reading today. The trend is flat at about 41, and the 40 to 41 step is within normal noise.

**Observations / suggestions.**
- The signals point to a poor night, not accumulated fatigue. Recovery time is about zero after the rest day, and the load ratio is optimal (1.0). Yet HRV is 38 ms, below the 45-55 baseline, resting HR is 53 (4 above the usual 49), and the 01:29 bedtime cut REM to 37 min. Today suits an easy aerobic session: a 40-50 min Z2 run, or an easy 1-1.5 h ride, with optional strides at the end.
- High-aerobic load is still the gap: 185 against a minimum of 409. The zone-4 threshold session is still the right fix, but postpone it until after a 7.5 h+ night with overnight HRV back above 45. Doing it today, on 6 h 24 min of sleep and suppressed HRV, would add stress without the quality.
- Both HRV dips to 38 ms (28 Sep and today) followed short nights under 6.5 h. An earlier bedtime is the cheapest lever for getting readiness back above 70.
